cls: Long-acting muscarinic antagonist (LAMA) - inhaled anticholinergic bronchodilator
quick: Two inhalations of one 18 mcg capsule (HandiHaler) once daily, or 2 actuations of 2.5 mcg Respimat once daily
Not relevant - inhaled only; do NOT swallow the capsules
Limited data; use only if benefit justifies potential risk
Unknown if excreted in human milk; use with caution
No dose adjustment, but monitor closely for anticholinergic effects if CrCl <=50 mL/min
Symptom/exacerbation control, inhaler technique, eye and urinary symptoms
summary: Tiotropium is a long-acting muscarinic antagonist (LAMA) given by inhalation for the long-term, once-daily maintenance treatment of COPD (chronic bronchitis and emphysema) and to reduce exacerbations. It is NOT a rescue inhaler and must not be used for acute bronchospasm. Capsules are for inhalation via the HandiHaler device only and must never be swallowed.
indications: Long-term, once-daily maintenance treatment of bronchospasm associated with COPD (chronic bronchitis and emphysema)
(Respimat) also indicated for long-term maintenance treatment of asthma in some approvals

dosage.d: Two inhalations of the powder of one 18 mcg capsule once daily via HandiHaler
dosage.n: Do not take more than one dose (one capsule) in 24 hours

dosage.d: Two actuations (2 x 2.5 mcg = 5 mcg) once daily
dosage.n: Same time each day; not for acute symptoms

admin: For oral inhalation only - DO NOT swallow the capsules
Use SPIRIVA capsules only with the HandiHaler device; pierce capsule and inhale the powder
Take at the same time each day; do not exceed one dose in 24 hours
Avoid getting powder or spray into the eyes (may precipitate or worsen narrow-angle glaucoma)
Not a rescue medication - have a short-acting bronchodilator available for acute symptoms
moa: Tiotropium is a long-acting antimuscarinic (anticholinergic) agent with similar affinity for muscarinic receptor subtypes M1 to M5. In the airways it inhibits M3 receptors on airway smooth muscle, producing bronchodilation. Its slow dissociation from M3 receptors gives a prolonged (>24 hour) duration of action allowing once-daily dosing.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to tiotropium, ipratropium, or any component of the product (including angioedema reported with prior use)
relative: Symptomatic prostatic hyperplasia or bladder-neck obstruction / urinary retention
Moderate to severe renal impairment (monitor closely)
monitor: Intraocular pressure / new or worsening glaucoma

preg: Limited human data are insufficient to establish a drug-associated risk. Animal studies showed post-implantation loss and fetal effects only at maternally toxic doses far above human exposure. Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
lact: It is not known whether tiotropium is excreted in human milk; it is present in milk of lactating rats. Consider the benefit of breastfeeding and the mother's clinical need, with caution.
renal: No dosage adjustment is required. However, because tiotropium is predominantly renally excreted, patients with moderate to severe renal impairment (CrCl <=50 mL/min) should be monitored closely for anticholinergic adverse effects.
hepatic: No dosage adjustment is required in hepatic impairment.

moderate: Other anticholinergic-containing drugs (additive anticholinergic effects - avoid coadministration, e.g. ipratropium)
minor: Has been used with beta-agonists, methylxanthines, and inhaled/oral steroids without increased adverse reactions
interactions.diagnostics: No clinically significant laboratory interference reported

rare: Immediate hypersensitivity reactions including angioedema (swelling of lips, tongue, throat)
emergency: Acute angle-closure glaucoma (acute eye pain, blurred vision, halos)

monitoring: COPD symptom control and exacerbation frequency
Signs of narrow-angle glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision, halos)
Urinary symptoms in men with prostatic hyperplasia
Renal function in patients with moderate-severe renal impairment
counsel: This is a maintenance inhaler taken once daily - it is NOT for sudden breathing trouble; use your rescue inhaler for that
Do not swallow the capsules; only use them with the HandiHaler device
Avoid getting the powder or spray in your eyes; if you get eye pain, blurred vision, or see halos, contact your doctor promptly
Report difficulty urinating, severe constipation, or sudden wheezing after a dose
Rinse mouth and maintain good technique to reduce dry mouth
pk: Bronchodilation within ~30 minutes of first dose
Steady-state peak FEV1 effect over the dosing interval; plasma peak ~5-7 minutes after inhalation
Terminal half-life approximately 25 hours after inhalation
Greater than 24 hours, supporting once-daily dosing
Store at 20-25 C (excursions 15-30 C); protect capsules from moisture; do not store capsules in the HandiHaler device; Respimat avoid freezing
pearls: LAMA used for maintenance, NOT rescue - patients must keep a short-acting bronchodilator for acute symptoms
Common mistake: patients swallowing the capsules instead of inhaling them via the HandiHaler
Slow M3-receptor dissociation gives its >24 h once-daily action ('kinetic selectivity')
Use cautiously in narrow-angle glaucoma, urinary retention, and prostatic hyperplasia due to anticholinergic effects
missed: If you miss your once-daily dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is almost time for the next day's dose, skip the missed dose - do not take two doses in 24 hours.
overdose: High doses may cause anticholinergic signs and symptoms (dry mouth, dry eyes/conjunctivitis, tachycardia, blurred vision, urinary retention, constipation, altered mental status). Systemic toxicity from inhaled use is unlikely because of low oral bioavailability; accidental swallowing of capsules is poorly absorbed. Treatment is discontinuation plus symptomatic and supportive care.
